subject: SOC2 Type II materials, interim attestation, and TrustLocker access
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Ortega <lucas.ortega@novamed.com>, Emma Holtz <emma.holtz@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-04T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: SOC2 Type II materials, interim attestation, and TrustLocker access

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today — great to meet the Novamed team. Quick recap and the items we discussed so you have a single list to share with Security/Legal.

Ask summary (what we need to move to procurement/compliance):
- Copy of the latest SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) or instructions for how you prefer we retrieve it from your portal.
- Interim/temporary attestation or bridge letter if the Type II report is recent and you can provide a short-term statement of controls.
- TrustLocker/portal access for secure upload of artifacts (or invite email if you host).
- Completed vendor DDQ / answers to the attached vendor questionnaire (we can accept either a PDF or a share link).
- Confirmation of DPA path (DocuSign link preferred) and any specific GDPR/HIPAA controls to note.

I attached a short interim attestation template we use as an example — feel free to swap in your wording. If it's easier for your team, you can invite redwood-security@redwood.com to the portal and we'll pull materials directly.

Proposed next steps:
1) If you can provision TrustLocker access, send the invite to security@redwood.com (CC me).
2) Upload SOC 2 Type II report and bridge letter (if available).
3) Confirm DPA route; if DocuSign, send the envelope link; if legal prefers redline, send to legal@redwood.com.

Target timeline: We typically need artifacts within 7 business days to keep the procurement cadence for early Q2. If that timeline is tight, let us know the expected date and we'll adjust the rollout plan.

Attachments referenced: [Attachment: redwood_temp_attestation.pdf (PDF, 18 KB) — sample interim attestation template]

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to hop on a 15-min follow-up if that helps coordinate internally.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0132 | diego.fernandez@redwood.com
[Redwood Inference — secure inference for production]

From: Lucas Ortega <lucas.ortega@novamed.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Novamed Security <security@novamed.com>, Emma Holtz <emma.holtz@novamed.com>
Date: 2028-03-05T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 Type II materials, interim attestation, and TrustLocker access

Thanks Diego — good talk earlier. We can help with the items below. A few notes from our side: 

- SOC 2 Type II: We have a hosted report in our TrustLocker instance. We can either share a view-access link or export a PDF. Which do you prefer?
- Bridge letter / interim attestation: We can provide an interim attestation, but it typically needs review by our InfoSec director. Expect a 2–3 business day turnaround.
- DPA / GDPR / HIPAA: Our legal team prefers DocuSign for the DPA. I'll request the DocuSign envelope and send the link to you. 
- Vendor DDQ: We received your questionnaire; attaching our DPO contact details and a minimal answers sheet to speed things up.

Attachments: [Attachment: Novamed_DPO_contact.pdf (PDF, 12 KB)], [Attachment: Novamed_vendorddq_answers.xlsx (XLSX, 32 KB) — sent via secure link]

Quick question: Does Redwood require encrypted upload or specific filename conventions in TrustLocker (for example: accountname_report_type_YYYY)? We want to make the upload process clean for both teams.

I'll aim to send the DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow.

—Lucas
Lucas Ortega
Head of IT Security, Novamed
lucas.ortega@novamed.com | +1 617-555-0222

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Ortega <lucas.ortega@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-05T11:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 Type II materials, interim attestation, and TrustLocker access

Appreciate the quick reply, Lucas. Either portal view-link or PDF works for us; view-access is great because it ensures we're seeing the most recent artifact. If you choose view-access, please include an expiration of at least 30 days.

Regarding upload conventions: a simple filename convention helps our compliance ops team — we generally suggest: novamed_soc2_typeii_YYYYMM.pdf and novamed_bridgeletter_YYYYMM.pdf. Encrypted upload is preferred; TrustLocker links with TLS plus pre-authenticated invite are fine (we'll also add an S3-backed intake if needed).

I attached the interim attestation we mentioned earlier so your InfoSec director has a starting point.

Next steps from our side:
- Marissa (CC) will coordinate with Compliance Ops to receive the TrustLocker invite and track the artifact intake.
- Priyom/Legal will be on standby for the DPA DocuSign review.

If you send the DocuSign link, please copy legal@redwood.com and compliance@redwood.com so we can triage quickly.

Thanks — I'll look out for the portal invite and the DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Diego
[Attachment: redwood_temp_attestation.pdf (PDF, 18 KB) — reiterated]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Forwarding the Novamed thread — they said they'll provision view access in TrustLocker and send a DocuSign DPA link. Can Compliance Ops provision a temporary intake bucket and watch for uploads from trustlocker@novamed.com?

Checklist for Compliance Ops: 
- Create intake record under deal DL-4921 (Novamed).
- Allowview access for two emails: security@novamed.com and trustlocker@novamed.com (if they send invites).
- Monitor and mark items on receipt: SOC2 PDF, bridge letter, vendor DDQ spreadsheet, DPO contact.
- If DocuSign DPA arrives, route to Priyom for legal review and to compliance@redwood.com for retention policy tagging.

Marissa Cole
